# AI migrations

> Case studies of software migrations done with AI: what worked, what failed, and which part AI did versus rule-based tools and people. Lessons drawn from them by aspect (planning, testing, review, rollout, cost and more), and a before-you-migrate checklist an agent runs on a repository.

Unofficial; company names describe the subject only. Every lesson comes from migrations; many apply to large engineering work done with AI agents generally, and those marked "Old system as oracle: no" carry over as they are. Each case says how far its claims can be checked and what stake its author has in the tools: weigh it accordingly.

## How to use

- Before a migration: run the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md) on the repository and change nothing. Each question has a Check to measure and cites lesson IDs; open only the lessons and cases behind a gap.
- For any other large piece of AI-driven work: pick the 2-3 aspect pages below that match it and read only those (one line per lesson, then its cases, the evidence against it, and its oracle and strength).
- Open a case only when you need its detail. Each has "Who did what", "How it was checked", a Numbers table with the basis of each number, "What went wrong" and "Practices to copy". File format: [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/AGENTS.md).
- Relative links inside these files resolve against https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/.

## Lessons

- [Planning and scoping](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/planning.md): 9 lessons, PLN-n (7 stated, 2 ours; oracle: 1 yes, 1 partly, 7 no). How to size, slice, order and stage a large piece of AI-driven work before agents touch the code.
- [Testing and oracles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/testing.md): 10 lessons, TST-n (8 stated, 2 ours; oracle: 7 yes, 2 partly, 1 no). What tells you the new code is right, and where those oracles fail.
- [Verification loops and gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/verification.md): 9 lessons, VER-n (9 stated, 0 ours; oracle: 1 yes, 6 partly, 2 no). The automated checks around each agent change, and what they can and cannot prove.
- [Code review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/review.md): 10 lessons, REV-n (8 stated, 2 ours; oracle: 2 yes, 4 partly, 4 no). How agent-written changes were reviewed, by agents and by people.
- [Release and rollout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): 7 lessons, ROL-n (6 stated, 1 ours; oracle: 2 yes, 2 partly, 3 no). How the new code reached users, and how risk was limited on the way.
- [Machines and operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/operations.md): 7 lessons, OPS-n (6 stated, 1 ours; oracle: 1 yes, 2 partly, 4 no). Running many agents on real machines, and keeping the result healthy after merge.
- [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/security.md): 10 lessons, SEC-n (7 stated, 3 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 3 partly, 7 no). Sandboxing agents, memory safety, dependencies and data integrity.
- [Cost](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/cost.md): 9 lessons, CST-n (3 stated, 6 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 1 partly, 8 no). Tokens, money, people's time and the bill after merge.
- [Team and roles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/team.md): 4 lessons, TEM-n (4 stated, 0 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 0 partly, 4 no). Who does what when agents write most of the code.
- [Rule-based tools and AI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/tooling.md): 6 lessons, TOL-n (6 stated, 0 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 2 partly, 4 no). Splitting the work between deterministic tools and models.
- [Context and prompts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): 9 lessons, CTX-n (9 stated, 0 ours; oracle: 1 yes, 2 partly, 6 no). What goes into the model's context, and how prompts are written.
- [Many agents at once](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/orchestration.md): 6 lessons, ORC-n (6 stated, 0 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 2 partly, 4 no). Running several agents in parallel without them wrecking each other.
- [Agent failure modes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/agent-failures.md): 8 lessons, AGF-n (7 stated, 1 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 1 partly, 7 no). How agents went wrong, so a plan can expect it.
- [Human oversight](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/oversight.md): 3 lessons, OVS-n (3 stated, 0 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 1 partly, 2 no). Where people stay in the loop, and what they guard.
- [Knowledge capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/knowledge.md): 3 lessons, KNW-n (3 stated, 0 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 1 partly, 2 no). Turning failures and logs into lasting improvements.
- [Measuring and reading results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/measurement.md): 9 lessons, MSR-n (3 stated, 6 ours; oracle: 0 yes, 2 partly, 7 no). How to read the numbers in these sources, and how to report your own.

## Cases

- [GitHub moves its Copilot agent runtime from TypeScript to Rust using agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md) — language, TypeScript on Node.js and V8 to Rust (native library with a C ABI); evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$120,000 for ~136.3 billion tokens (engineer time not priced). One engineer steered agent fleets to port about 430,000 lines of TypeScript to Rust in place, one component per PR, over 14.5 weeks.
- [Intel's IDEAS harness ports the libgit2 command-line client from C to safe Rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md) — language, C (libgit2 command-line client) to safe Rust (no unsafe code); evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$0.55 per symbol for translation (total unstated), plus ~$6.5 for repair. An LLM harness turned 112K lines of C into safe Rust that compiled but crashed; 8 person-hours guiding an agent got git blame working.
- [Bun moves its JavaScript runtime off Zig onto Rust with Claude agents in 11 days](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md) — language, Zig (Bun runtime, bundler, package manager, test runner) to Rust (about 100 crates); evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$165,000 at API list prices for the tokens used before merge (690 million output tokens, 5.9 billion fresh input tokens, 72 billion cached input tokens). One engineer ran about 50 Claude Code workflows, up to 64 agents at once, to port 535K lines of Zig to Rust; all tests passed and it merged in 11 days.
- [1Password uses AI agents to refactor its Go monolith and begin a service extraction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md) — architecture, Go monolith (B5), database transactions opened with MustBegin (panics on failure) to separately owned services; transaction calls that return errors; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents rewrote over 3,000 panicking transaction calls from a tight spec, but stumbled on a service extraction's ordering and invariants.
- [Spotify runs fleet-wide migrations with its Honk background coding agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md) — mixed, many (for example Java AutoValue classes, old Scio versions, deprecated datasets) to many (for example Java records, the newest Scio, new dataset versions); evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. Spotify put a coding agent inside its fleet migration tooling; verifiers and an LLM judge gate each PR, and over 1,500 agent PRs were merged.
- [Google widens int32 IDs to int64 in 39 migrations with an LLM pipeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md) — data, int32 ID fields in protocol buffer schemas and the code using them (Java, C++, Dart and others) to int64 ID fields; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. A nightly pipeline of code search, rule-based sorting, an internal Gemini model and staged checks drafted 74.45% of 595 code changes in 39 ID migrations.
- [Airbnb moves 3.5K React test files off Enzyme onto React Testing Library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React component tests) to React Testing Library; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. An LLM pipeline with per-file validation steps and retries migrated 97% of about 3,500 React test files; people finished the rest by hand.
- [Slack pairs a syntax-tree codemod with Claude 2.1 to help move 15K Enzyme tests to React Testing Library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React unit and integration tests) to React Testing Library; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Codemod alone 45% (evaluation files), Claude 2.1 alone 40-60% (base not given), both 80% of code in 9 checked files; 22% of tests passed over 338 files.

## Optional

- [Every lesson in one file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms-full.txt): for tools that cannot follow links. About 93 KB (~24k tokens), so prefer the aspect pages when you can.
- [Pitfalls by kind of move](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/pitfalls.md): what the old stack did implicitly, and seams for moving in steps.
- [Lessons index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/index.md): counts, the cases behind each lesson, and where the cases disagree.
